proposed_statement_changes.proposed: On the fixed known support \(H\) defining \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), is the uniform excess-endpoint rate \(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2}\) minimax, up to logarithmic factors, along sequences of laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) for which \(R(P)\to0\)? More sharply, can a matching lower bound distinguish the cost of estimating the obstacle boundary from the cost of estimating the signed objective? A shrinking support-hole transition lies outside \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) and requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current question combines two regimes that the frozen class cannot contain. By \(H=\bigcup_{R\in\mathscr R}R\) for the fixed known rectangle family \(\mathscr R\) and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) on \(H\), every law in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) has the same support topology. Thus \(R(P)\to0\) is a legitimate fixed-support transition, whereas an approaching conditional-support hole requires a new varying-support class. The proposed wording narrows the open question to the regime represented by the existing primitives and explicitly separates the unsupported regime.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), the support is the fixed known rectangle union \(H\) and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) on \(H\), so a shrinking conditional-support hole is not an admissible path. Study minimax excess-endpoint risk along fixed-support sequences of laws \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) with \(R(P)\to0\) by constructing and verifying Le Cam two-point or Assouad families of \(\beta\)-H\"older perturbations of \(g\) and/or \(\nu_P\) that preserve every class restriction and separate the optimized endpoints of \(\Theta(P)\). A support-topology transition must instead be posed on a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class with explicit geometry and density conditions. This handle asserts no lower bound.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The old handle proposed a shrinking support hole inside a class whose fixed known rectangle support and uniform positive density lower bound rule out that construction. The corrected handle separates the admissible fixed-support \(R(P)\to0\) problem from a future varying-support problem and makes clear that constructing a valid least-favorable family remains the crux.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A matching minimax lower bound, uniform along fixed-support sequences in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) with \(R(P)\to0\), that separately attributes endpoint loss to estimating the obstacle boundary and to estimating the signed objective; any support-topology transition additionally requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
open_obligations.obstruction: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), \(H=\bigcup_{R\in\mathscr R}R\) is the same known finite rectangle union and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) throughout \(H\). Hence the suggested shrinking-hole family is outside the frozen class. Within fixed \(H\), the primitives establish the upper bound but supply no verified two-point or hypercube family that simultaneously remains in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\), has bounded product-experiment divergence, preserves nonempty obstacle feasibility, and separates an optimized WAOSS endpoint at the asserted rate.
open_obligations.attempted: The natural route perturbs \(g\) by a local \(\beta\)-H\"older bump and perturbs \(\nu_P\) to isolate the two error sources. A shrinking hole violates fixed support; on fixed support, verifying the density bounds, outcome bounds, obstacle compatibility, divergence bound, and optimized-endpoint separation is precisely the missing least-favorable-family construction. Assuming those properties would assume the crux.
open_obligations.partial_result: The established theorem gives the uniform upper endpoint error \(O(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2})\). Moreover, the support restriction itself yields a sharp scope conclusion: because \(H\) is the fixed known rectangle union and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\) on it, support topology cannot approach failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\). Therefore the current minimax problem can vary \(R(P)\to0\) only on fixed \(H\); a shrinking-hole lower bound belongs to a new varying-support class. No matching fixed-support lower bound or decomposition into obstacle and signed-objective costs follows from the frozen primitives.

prose_updates.tldr: The marginal quasi-stayer condition in Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024) does not identify its weighted WAOSS singleton: at the regular heterogeneous-baseline witness, the published completion class admits an affine recession ray and its WAOSS image is all of \(\mathbb R\). Only this negative result transfers directly to the published class. The positive result is a sharp bounded-slope and Lipschitz sensitivity analysis on a strengthened completion class that additionally imposes the \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and continuity of \(g\); its attained obstacle interval is not the source-class identified set. Baseline-conditional zero support collapses that interval to the weighted singleton formula in the proceedings theorem, while arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 remains only an analogous result for the distinct unweighted target \(\delta_1\). The explicit finite program yields a uniformly honest outer interval on the fixed-support regular subclass. Minimaxity remains open for \(R(P)\to0\) on fixed \(H\); shrinking support holes require a separate varying-support class.

project_justification.gap: The proceedings paper states weighted WAOSS point identification under Assumptions 1--4, but its marginal quasi-stayer condition does not imply the baseline-conditional positivity used immediately before display (4) of its Appendix proof. The regular witness is decisive: over the published completion class, a legal affine recession ray makes the WAOSS image equal to \(\mathbb R\). Thus the published-class singleton fails, and a finite interval cannot be represented as that class's identified set.
project_justification.niche: The class distinction creates the paper's central elbow. The published class remains unbounded at the witness. The positive obstacle geometry instead belongs to a strengthened sensitivity class with continuous \(g\), bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and the \(K|\Delta D|\) conditional mean-movement bound. On observed laws satisfying the source assumptions this is a restricted slice of the source completions, but there is no unconditional global equality or inclusion between the classes because their maintained conditions and domains differ.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the published-class unbounded-ray counterexample, then gives an exact full-observed-law sharp interval only for the strengthened bounded-slope and Lipschitz sensitivity class. It proves attained interval geometry, point identification exactly when \(R(P)=0\), recovery of the proceedings weighted formula under baseline-conditional support, obstacle clipping, certified finite programs, and uniform outer coverage on a fixed rectangle-support subclass. The common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval is retained only as prior-art sanity check, and the source's separate parametric estimator is not challenged.

sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed two-period panel sampling from \(P\). Population statements distinguish the proceedings paper's Assumptions 1--4 completion class from the strengthened bounded-slope and Lipschitz sensitivity class used for the positive sharp interval.
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units have observed \(Y_1,Y_2,D_1,D_2\) and one-argument static potential-outcome schedules on the known compact interval \(I\). The simultaneous conditional-parallel-trends clause uses one common full-probability event over all baseline doses, so evaluation at the random baseline is legitimate.
sampling_model.treatment: Baseline and follow-up doses are continuous and exact stayers are excluded. The root sensitivity theorem does not require marginal quasi-stayers. Its completion class adds the \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and continuity of \(g\); it is not globally equal to or nested with the published Assumptions 1--4 class. Conditional on an observed law satisfying the source assumptions, it is only a restricted slice of source completions.
sampling_model.overlap: Population sensitivity analysis permits arbitrary compact observed support \(H\). Uniform inference fixes a known finite rectangle union \(H\), imposes \(f_0\le f_{XZ}\le f_1\), and requires \(A\ge a_0\). These fixed restrictions rule out support topology approaching failure within \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A deterministic rectangle-subordinate cell-mean estimator of \(g\) is combined with the signed empirical measure for \(\nu_P\), Hoeffding bands for \(T\) and \(A\), and a component-respecting finite outer ratio program. The simultaneous event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\) yields uniform outer coverage and the displayed upper rate. A matching lower bound is open for fixed-support sequences with \(R(P)\to0\); support-hole sequences require a new varying-support class.

prose_updates.related_work: de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024, Assumptions 1--4, Theorem 1, and the Appendix argument immediately before display (4)) state a weighted WAOSS singleton using marginal quasi-stayers, although the proof invokes baseline-conditional positivity. The regular heterogeneous-baseline witness shows more than failure of that proof step: the published completion class admits a legal affine recession ray and its WAOSS image is \(\mathbb R\). This non-representability result, and not the positive finite interval, transfers to the published class. The bounded-slope and Lipschitz sharp interval is a sensitivity repair on a strengthened class adding continuous \(g\), bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and the \(K|\Delta D|\) conditional mean-movement restriction. There is no global equality or inclusion between this class and the source class; for observed laws satisfying the source assumptions, the sensitivity completions form only a restricted slice. Under baseline-conditional support, the sensitivity interval collapses to the weighted formula in the 2024 proceedings theorem. By contrast, de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1, Assumption 5 and Theorem 3) provide an analogous conditional-support result for the distinct unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\). de Chaisemartin, Ciccia, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Knau (2024, Section 4.2.1, Theorem 4, and Appendix B.2 of arXiv:2405.04465v4) already establish the common-zero-baseline scalar bounded-slope interval, which is used only as an algebraic sanity check. Freyberger and Horowitz (2015), Freyberger (2017), and Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018) inform finite shape-restricted and signed-support optimization. Belloni et al. (2015), Cattaneo et al. (2024), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Voronin (2025) inform the inference ingredients; the proved theorem supplies their uniform composition here. Sasaki and Ura (2025) inform the slow-mover comparison but retain point identification. None of these comparisons supplies the still-open fixed-support minimax lower bound. The proceedings paper's separate parametric estimator is not invalidated by the nonparametric identification counterexample.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform theorem is tied to a fixed known rectangle union, fixed \(\beta\), positive density lower bound, bounded outcomes, denominator separation, and the conservative cell-mean radius. It proves boundary-cell coverage, signed empirical-process control, measurable finite-program endpoints, and ratio propagation on \(\mathcal E_n(P)\), but not minimax optimality. Because \(H\) is fixed and \(f_{XZ}\ge f_0>0\), this class cannot encode a support topology approaching failure. The remaining in-class question is a matching lower bound as \(R(P)\to0\) on fixed \(H\); a shrinking-hole transition requires a separately defined varying-support triangular-array class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The negative published-class conclusion is exact at the regular witness: under the source's Assumptions 1--4, the completion ray yields every WAOSS value in \(\mathbb R\), so the claimed nonparametric singleton is not identified there. The positive sharp set \(\Theta(P)\) belongs only to the strengthened sensitivity class with the \(K\) mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, and continuous \(g\). No global equality or inclusion with the published class is claimed; on observed laws satisfying the source assumptions, the sensitivity class is merely a restricted slice, and its finite interval does not transfer upward. Baseline-conditional zero support recovers the proceedings paper's weighted singleton formula. Theorem 3 of arXiv:2201.06898v1 remains an analogous conditional-support result for unweighted \(\delta_1\), and the common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval from arXiv:2405.04465v4 is prior art used only as a sanity check. The source's separate parametric estimator is not invalidated. Uniform outer inference is proved only for the fixed known rectangle-support, fixed-H\"older, bounded-density, bounded-outcome, denominator-separated subclass. Minimaxity is open as \(R(P)\to0\) on fixed \(H\); unknown or varying support, shrinking support holes, adaptive smoothness, vanishing \(A\), carry-over, clustered sampling, bounded counterfactual levels, and optimal interval length are outside the claim.

proofs.proof_tex:
Compactness of \(I\) and the support condition give \(|Z|\leq\operatorname{diam}(I)\) almost surely. The no-stayer condition gives \(|Z|>0\) almost surely. Consequently
\[
0<A=E_P|Z|\leq\operatorname{diam}(I)<\infty.
\]
Observed integrability implies \(E_P|\Delta Y|<\infty\), and hence \(T=E_P[S\Delta Y]\) is finite because \(|S|=1\) almost surely.

Take \(Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\) and put \(m=m_Q\). Consistency gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta Y
&=Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\\
&=\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}
  +\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The simultaneous clause in conditional parallel trends provides one \(Q\)-full event on which its conditional-mean equality holds for every \(d\in X_0\). Since \(D_1=X\in X_0\) almost surely, evaluation on the diagonal \(d=X\) is therefore legitimate and yields
\[
E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z\right]=m(X).
\]
Taking the conditional expectation of the preceding decomposition, using the observed-law match and the declared support version of \(g\), gives
\[
g(x,z)-m(x)
=E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\mid X=x,Z=z\right]
\]
for \(P_{XZ}\)-almost every \((x,z)\). The conditional mean-movement bound therefore implies
\[
|g(x,z)-m(x)|\leq K|z|
\qquad P_{XZ}\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]
The function \((x,z)\mapsto |g(x,z)-m(x)|-K|z|\) is continuous on \(H\): continuity of \(g\) is assumed and \(m\in C(X_0)\) is part of the legal-completion definition. If it were positive at any point of \(H=\operatorname{supp}_P(X,Z)\), it would remain positive on a relatively open neighborhood having positive \(P_{XZ}\)-probability, contradicting the almost-everywhere inequality. Hence
\[
|g(x,z)-m(x)|\leq K|z|\qquad\text{for every }(x,z)\in H.
\]
Together with the trend bound and the global Lipschitz condition in \(\mathfrak Q(P)\), this proves \(m\in\mathcal C_P\), and hence
\[
\mathfrak Q(P)\neq\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing.
\]

The same decomposition identifies the causal functional without defining it to equal an observed functional. By iterated expectations, the diagonal equality above, and the definition of the signed measure \(\nu_P\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
A\theta(Q)
&=E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
&=E_P[S\Delta Y]
  -E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
&=T-E_P[S m(X)]\\
&=T-\int_{X_0}m(x)\,d\nu_P(x)
=T-J_P(m).
\end{aligned}
\]
The integrals are finite because \(m\) is bounded. Thus every value generated by \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) belongs to \(\Theta(P)\).

Conversely, fix \(u\in\mathcal C_P\) and retain the observed vector with law \(P\). On \(\{Z\neq0\}\), define
\[
b_u=\frac{g(X,Z)-u(X)}{Z},
\]
and put \(b_u=0\) on the \(P\)-null event \(\{Z=0\}\). Measurability follows from the continuity, hence Borel measurability, of \(g\) and \(u\) on their supports. The support inequalities defining \(\mathcal C_P\) give
\[
|b_u|\leq K\qquad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Define simultaneously for all \(d\in I\)
\[
Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=Y_1+b_u(d-D_1),
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)=Y_2+b_u(d-D_2).
\]
These are jointly measurable static schedules. They satisfy consistency pointwise:
\[
Y_1^{Q_u}(D_1)=Y_1,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)=Y_2.
\]
Therefore the entire joint observed law remains \(P\), not merely a collection of its moments. For every fixed \(d\in I\), compactness of \(I\), the bound on \(b_u\), and observed integrability give
\[
|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|\leq |Y_t|+K\operatorname{diam}(I),
\qquad
E_{Q_u}|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|<\infty.
\]
For every \(d,d'\in I\),
\[
|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)-Y_t^{Q_u}(d')|
=|b_u|\,|d-d'|
\leq K|d-d'|,
\]
so both schedules are individually \(K\)-Lipschitz.

Their period difference does not depend on the dose argument:
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)
&=\Delta Y+b_u(D_1-D_2)\\
&=\Delta Y-b_uZ\\
&=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)
\end{aligned}
\]
for every \(d\in I\), on one common event. Since \(g(X,Z)=E_P[\Delta Y\mid X,Z]\), this identity implies, simultaneously for every \(d\in I\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X,Z]
&=u(X),\\
E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X]
&=u(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the strengthened all-\(I\) parallel-trends equality holds, including its diagonal clause, and the displayed version gives \(m_{Q_u}=u\) on \(X_0\). The bound and Lipschitz restrictions on \(m_{Q_u}\) follow from \(u\in\mathcal C_P\). Moreover,
\[
Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)
=b_uZ
=g(X,Z)-u(X),
\]
and therefore
\[
\left|E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)\mid X,Z]\right|
\leq K|Z|.
\]
All defining conditions of \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) are now verified, so \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\). This proves the reverse nonemptiness implication. Finally,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta(Q_u)
&=\frac{E_P[S\{g(X,Z)-u(X)\}]}{A}\\
&=\frac{T-J_P(u)}{A},
\end{aligned}
\]
because iterated expectations give \(E_P[Sg(X,Z)]=E_P[S\Delta Y]=T\). Every point of \(\Theta(P)\) is therefore attained by a legal full-data law, while the first half of the proof excludes every other value.

The assumptions used in this argument are exactly the displayed dependencies: marginal quasi-stayers never enter. The finite movement bound, bounded globally Lipschitz trend, continuous support version, and simultaneous diagonal clause are additional restrictions relative to the published model. Consequently the proved set equality is confined to \(\mathfrak Q(P)\); it cannot be transferred to a larger completion class merely because both classes satisfy the source's basic causal restrictions.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\) be the published Assumptions 1--4 completion class and let \(Q_c^{\circ}\) be the affine completion generated by \(c\in\mathbb R\) and \(\phi\). The law \(P^{\circ}\) has a bounded density that is strictly positive on each rectangle of its finite rectangle support and has uniformly bounded observed outcomes. It satisfies marginal quasi-stayers, whereas baseline-conditional positivity fails for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), a region of \(P^{\circ}_X\)-probability \(p_{\circ}\). For every finite \(c\), \(Q_c^{\circ}\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\), its schedules are affine and integrable, it preserves the entire observed law, and it satisfies parallel trends simultaneously for every \(d\in[-2,2]\). Moreover,
\[
\theta(Q_c^{\circ})=-\frac{3c p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
\qquad
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\}=\mathbb R.
\]
For the strengthened sensitivity class with \(K=L=M=1\), \(Q_+^{\circ}=Q_1^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}=Q_{-1}^{\circ}\) attain the endpoints
\[
\Theta(P^{\circ})=
\left[-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
       \frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}\right].
\]
Thus the identification elbow has three distinct stages: the unrestricted published class gives all of \(\mathbb R\) at this regular witness; the bounded-slope/Lipschitz class gives the displayed finite obstacle interval; and, under baseline-conditional zero support, the obstacle restriction fixes \(u(x)=g(x,0)\) and yields the published weighted singleton formula. Only the negative conclusion for the published singleton transfers to the published class; the finite interval does not.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The first rectangle in the definition of \(P^{\circ}\) has area \(1/2\) and density \(2p_{\circ}\), so it has probability \(p_{\circ}\). The second also has area \(1/2\) and has density \(2(1-p_{\circ})\), so it has probability \(1-p_{\circ}\). Since \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), the density is bounded and strictly positive on each of the two rectangles. The observed outcomes are zero and hence uniformly bounded. Absolute continuity gives \(P^{\circ}(Z=0)=0\). The second rectangle contains treatment changes arbitrarily close to zero with positive Lebesgue measure, and therefore
\[
P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta)>0\qquad\text{for every }\eta>0.
\]
In contrast, for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), the conditional support of \(Z\) is \([1/2,1]\), whence
\[
P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta\mid X=x)=0
\qquad\text{for }0<\eta<1/2.
\]
The marginal density of \(X\) on \([-1,0]\) is \(p_{\circ}\), so the failure region has \(P_X^{\circ}\)-probability \(p_{\circ}\).

Fix a finite \(c\in\mathbb R\). On the first rectangle, \(|\phi(X)|\leq1/2\leq |Z|\), while on the second rectangle \(\phi(X)=0\). Thus, off the null event \(\{Z=0\}\),
\[
\left|\frac{c\phi(X)}{Z}\right|\leq |c|.
\]
Because \(D_1,D_2,d\in[-2,2]\), both schedules in the definition of \(Q_c^{\circ}\) are bounded in absolute value by \(4|c|\) for every fixed \(d\). They are therefore integrable, affine in \(d\), and have everywhere finite slope. At the realized treatments,
\[
Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_1)=0=Y_1,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_2)=0=Y_2.
\]
Consequently consistency holds and the complete observed vector retains law \(P^{\circ}\).

For every \(d\in[-2,2]\), direct subtraction gives, on the same event for all \(d\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)
&=-\frac{c\phi(X)}{Z}\{(d-D_2)-(d-X)\}\\
&=c\phi(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
The right-hand side is measurable with respect to \(X\). Hence
\[
E_{Q_c^{\circ}}[Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)\mid X,Z]
=c\phi(X)
=E_{Q_c^{\circ}}[Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)\mid X]
\]
simultaneously for every \(d\). This verifies the source parallel-trends clause, and in fact its stronger common-event version. The observed support clauses were verified above, so \(Q_c^{\circ}\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\).

The period-two causal movement is
\[
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_1)
=-c\phi(X).
\]
On the first rectangle \(S=1\). On the second rectangle, \(Z\) is conditionally uniform on the symmetric interval \([-1/4,1/4]\), and \(\phi(X)=0\) there in any event. Therefore
\[
E_{P^{\circ}}[S\phi(X)]
=p_{\circ}\int_{-1}^0\min\{-x,1/2\}\,dx
=\frac{3p_{\circ}}8.
\]
Also,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{P^{\circ}}|Z|
&=p_{\circ}\,E[Z\mid Z\in[1/2,1]]
 +(1-p_{\circ})E[|Z|\mid Z\in[-1/4,1/4]]\\
&=\frac{3p_{\circ}}4+\frac{1-p_{\circ}}8
=\frac{1+5p_{\circ}}8.
\end{aligned}
\]
It follows from the causal definition, rather than by definition of an observed functional, that
\[
\theta(Q_c^{\circ})
=\frac{-cE_{P^{\circ}}[S\phi(X)]}{E_{P^{\circ}}|Z|}
=-\frac{3cp_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}.
\]
The multiplier \(3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})\) is strictly positive. As \(c\) ranges over \(\mathbb R\), these values range over all of \(\mathbb R\), proving
\[
\mathbb R\subseteq
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\}.
\]
The reverse inclusion is immediate from the definition of the source completion class, which requires the causal movement defining \(\theta(Q)\) to be integrable, so every \(\theta(Q)\) is a finite real number. This proves equality.

It remains to calculate the middle, bounded-sensitivity stage. Because \(\Delta Y=0\), the continuous support version is \(g=0\). For \(K=L=M=1\), every \(u\in\mathcal C_{P^{\circ}}\) obeys \(u(x)=0\) on \([0,1]\), since \((x,0)\in H\) there. On \([-1,0]\), the support contains \((x,1/2)\), so the obstacle restriction gives \(|u(x)|\leq1/2\). Global one-Lipschitz continuity and \(u(0)=0\) also give \(|u(x)|\leq -x\). Hence
\[
|u(x)|\leq\phi(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in[-1,1].
\]
Both \(\phi\) and \(-\phi\) are continuous, bounded by one, globally one-Lipschitz, and satisfy every support obstacle, so both belong to \(\mathcal C_{P^{\circ}}\).

On the first rectangle \(S=1\), whereas on the second rectangle the conditional sign mean is zero. It follows that
\[
d\nu_{P^{\circ}}(x)
=p_{\circ}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\}\,dx.
\]
Consequently
\[
-\frac{3p_{\circ}}8
\leq J_{P^{\circ}}(u)
\leq\frac{3p_{\circ}}8,
\]
and the two bounds are attained by \(-\phi\) and \(\phi\), respectively. Since \(T=0\) and \(A=(1+5p_{\circ})/8\), full-law sharpness and the attained-interval theorem give
\[
\Theta(P^{\circ})
=\left[-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
        \frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}\right].
\]
The definitions show \(Q_+^{\circ}=Q_1^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}=Q_{-1}^{\circ}\), so these two completions attain the lower and upper endpoints, respectively.

Finally, if baseline-conditional zero support is imposed so that \((x,0)\in H\) at every relevant baseline \(x\), the defining obstacle at \((x,0)\) reads
\[
|g(x,0)-u(x)|\leq K|0|=0.
\]
Thus every compatible \(u\) equals the observed trend \(g(\cdot,0)\), and the bounded-class set reduces to
\[
\left\{\frac{T-\int_{X_0}g(x,0)\,d\nu_P(x)}{A}\right\}.
\]
This proves the stated three-stage elbow and also shows why the finite sensitivity interval cannot be promoted to the unrestricted published completion class.
added_lemmas.justification: The affine recession ray proves that the published-class failure is unbounded, while the bounded-slope/Lipschitz model has a finite sharp interval.
added_lemmas.gap: Marginal quasi-stayers do not supply the baseline-conditional support used before display (4) in the proof of the published theorem; the regular witness makes the resulting source-class identified set equal to \(\mathbb R\).
added_lemmas.consumer: The result separates the invalid published singleton, the finite sensitivity interval under explicit bounds, and recovery of the weighted singleton under conditional zero support.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under the observed-law conditions and the simultaneous conditional-parallel-trends condition on the baseline-treatment support \(X_0\), the bounded-slope/Lipschitz completion class \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is nonempty if and only if \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\). Whenever these sets are nonempty,
\[
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}=\Theta(P).
\]
For every \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), the affine one-argument static-schedule lift produces \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), preserves the entire joint law \(P\), satisfies \(m_{Q_u}=u\in C(X_0)\), and makes both period schedules individually \(K\)-Lipschitz. Moreover, on one common full-probability event,
\[
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)\qquad\text{for every }d\in I,
\]
so the lift satisfies the stronger all-\(I\) parallel-trends equality and \(\theta(Q_u)=\{T-J_P(u)\}/A\). This theorem does not require marginal quasi-stayers. Its model is not the class defined by Assumptions 1--4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024): the theorem additionally imposes the finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, continuity of the observed regression version \(g\), and the simultaneous diagonal clause in parallel trends. Thus no equality or global inclusion of the two observed-law models is asserted. On an observed law that satisfies the published assumptions, \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is only the restricted slice satisfying these extra conditions, and \(\Theta(P)\) is not asserted to be the published-class identified set. The result is a sharp bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity repair after failure of the published singleton claim, not a sharp characterization of the unrestricted published class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The existing comparative sentence incorrectly presents sharpness for the strengthened bounded-slope/Lipschitz completion slice as an extension of the unrestricted published class. The corrected claim preserves the proved sharp equality but confines it to the declared sensitivity class, makes the simultaneous diagonal clause explicit, records that marginal quasi-stayers are unused, and disclaims transfer to the published-class identified set.

proposed.name: \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\)
proposed.construction:
Let \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\) denote the full-data completion class for the witness law under Assumptions 1--4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024): \(Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\) if the observed vector has law \(P^{\circ}\), \(d\mapsto Y_t^Q(d)\) is a one-argument static potential-outcome schedule on \(I=[-2,2]\), consistency holds, the potential outcomes and the causal movement defining \(\theta(Q)\) are integrable, and for each \(d\in[-1,1]\)
\[
E_Q[Y_2^Q(d)-Y_1^Q(d)\mid X,Z]
=E_Q[Y_2^Q(d)-Y_1^Q(d)\mid X]
\qquad Q\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The observed no-stayer and marginal quasi-stayer clauses are imposed through \(P^{\circ}\). Any source regularity requiring existence of a dose derivative is read literally; the affine schedules used below have an everywhere finite derivative for each completion. This class imposes no common finite bound \(K\) on causal movements and no common finite bounds \(L,M\) on baseline trends.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The published completion class must be an explicit object before its identified set can be contrasted with the strengthened sensitivity-class interval.

proposed.name: source-class affine recession ray
proposed.construction:
Define
\[
\phi(x)=\min\{-x,1/2\}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\},
\qquad x\in[-1,1].
\]
For every \(c\in\mathbb R\), retain the observed vector with law \(P^{\circ}\), and define the affine static schedules
\[
Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)=-\frac{c\phi(X)(d-X)}{Z},
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)=-\frac{c\phi(X)(d-D_2)}{Z},
\qquad d\in[-2,2],
\]
with both quotient terms set equal to zero on \(\{Z=0\}\). This construction defines \(Q_c^{\circ}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The unbounded source-class conclusion requires an explicit legal completion for every finite real ray index.

The two-point proposition is obsolete: the same regular witness supports an affine recession ray whose published-class identified set is all of \(\mathbb R\), while retaining the two bounded-class endpoint witnesses as the middle stage of the identification elbow.
